Apple has announced it will extend free access to its satellite features for existing iPhone users by another year, according to a footnote in the iPhone 18 Pro press release. Here are the details.

Apple Confirms Another Extension

Apple first introduced satellite connectivity with the iPhone 14 lineup, initially offering "Emergency SOS via satellite" and the ability to share your location via satellite through Find My. Apple said at the time that the free period would last for two years.

Apple has since expanded its satellite services to include features like Roadside Assistance via satellite and Messages via satellite. Apple now collectively refers to these features as satellite features.

In November 2023, Apple extended free access to Emergency SOS via satellite for existing iPhone 14 users by another year. Last year, Apple extended the free period once again, this time covering existing iPhone 14 and iPhone 15 users.

Without an extension, free access for some users would have expired later this year. However, Apple announced in a footnote of yesterday's iPhone 18 Pro press release that the free period will be extended by yet another year, and for the first time, existing iPhone 16 users will also be covered.

The original press release text reads:

Since Apple provides one year of free satellite features with every new iPhone purchase, this means buyers of the all-new iPhone 18 Pro, iPhone 18 Pro Max, and iPhone Duo will receive one year free, while existing iPhone 14, iPhone 15, and iPhone 16 users covered by the extension will also receive an additional year free.

Apple has not yet announced pricing for after the free period ends. Given that some of these features could be matters of life and death, many suspect Apple may ultimately keep at least some of them free, as charging users for emergency services could prove controversial.

Regardless, free access has been extended for another year. Whether this will be the last extension, or whether we'll be reporting on something similar again next year, remains to be seen.

Do you think Apple will eventually charge for satellite features? Let us know in the comments.
